sources.title: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) - GeeksforGeeks
sources.snippet: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a way to make AI answers more reliable by combining searching for relevant information and then generating a response. Instead of guessing based only on old training data, it first finds useful data from external sources (like documents or databases) and then uses it to give a better answer.

sources.title: Retrieval-augmented generation - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. [1][2] With RAG, LLMs first refer to a specified set of documents, then respond to user queries.

sources.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): Enhance LLMs with Factual Data - IBM
sources.snippet: Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is an architectural pattern that enables foundation models to produce factually correct outputs for specialized or proprietary topics that were not part of the model's training data.
